description: At 13:24 on 14 October 2024 the R3 delivery carrier beam fell into the mill pit and struck the sled and scaffold. Investigate the physical mechanism and its relevant upstream causes, preserving evidence limits.

D01.title: R3 delivery carrier beam - initial event notice
D01.content:
D01.S01 Event
At 13:24 on 14 October 2024 the R3 delivery carrier beam fell into the mill pit and struck the sled and scaffold platform. No person was struck. The assembly had been parked raised after backup-roll removal during the outage.

D01.S02 Initial observations
The keeper plate was found bolted to the recovered assembly. The beam and yoke were not reported fractured. These are initial condition observations, not a conclusion about the release mechanism.

D01.S03 Available leads
A motion record, work package, isolation records, inspection photographs and hydraulic records have been retained. Their coverage and applicability must be checked. The cause of the event is not stated in this notice.

D02.title: R3 raised assembly - functional system description
D02.content:
D02.S01 Applicability
This functional description applies to R3 assembly set CB-3/YK-3 in the maintenance configuration with backup rolls removed. It specifies the equipment model used in this record set. It is not an operating or isolation instruction.

D02.S02 Load and fluid paths
Yoke YK-3 follows support cylinder C17 at a 1:1 vertical displacement ratio. The effective support area is 100 cm2. With no independent mechanical block, loss of support-chamber fluid permits downward yoke travel under load. The isolated test boundary has one chamber-to-return path through valve V17; external leakage and alternate return paths are separately monitored.

D02.S03 Position versus sealing
The V17 CLOSED limit switch detects handle position. It does not measure seat leakage. Motor/pump supply being isolated does not prove that the raised assembly is mechanically restrained or that trapped fluid cannot leave the chamber.

D02.S04 Geometry and interference
The carrier normally seats on the yoke. Mill post/spreader contact can temporarily hold the carrier vertically while the yoke moves down. Relative vertical withdrawal is yoke downward travel minus carrier downward travel over the same interval. Temporary interference contact is not a designed mechanical block.

D02.S05 Primary and secondary retention
In the defined seated starting state, primary vertical seating engagement is 30 mm. Relative downward withdrawal of the yoke of at least 30 mm eliminates that primary seating engagement. This rule does not prove that the keeper is bypassed. Keeper engagement additionally depends on lateral offset and the dynamic path; those conditions require their own evidence.

D02.S06 Energy
Gravity remains available while the assembly is raised. Electrical isolation, hydraulic handle position and positive mechanical restraint are distinct conditions. No rule here states that a leaking valve alone is sufficient to make the carrier fall.

D04.title: Stripper-box changeout - task isolation package
D04.content:
D04.S01 Scope
Task WP-031 covers stripper-box changeout with the balance assembly raised after backup-roll removal. The package calls for electrical supply isolation and hydraulic valve closure. The task text contains no instruction to install a positive yoke block or verify the off-center carrier retention envelope.

D04.S02 Circuit nomenclature
The cover calls the supply group B hydraulics. A worksheet calls support-chamber trapped energy A. These names are not circuit identities. Use the tag schedule: C17 support chamber and V17 return-isolation valve belong to the raised balance assembly. Do not substitute unrelated A/B circuit records based on the letter alone.

D04.S03 Interpretation limit
A procedural omission is distinct from proof of what workers did. Execution records are needed to establish whether a block was actually present. This document does not establish why the procedure omitted that step.

D15.title: Preliminary investigation note - unreviewed
D15.content:
D15.S01 Draft interpretation
The writer suggests that the closed valve indication proves hydraulic isolation and that the installed keeper should have prevented all movement. The writer therefore suspects excess clearance.

D15.S02 Basis and status
This note cites only the initial event notice and handle-status entry. It contains no leak measurement, retention-envelope calculation or independent witness account. Status: unreviewed interpretation, not an additional observation.

D15.S03 Source lineage
The attached action summary was copied from the initial investigation meeting. Repetition in this note is not independent corroboration.

D07.title: CAM-3 motion measurement and coverage report
D07.content:
D07.S01 Record identity
Source CAM-3, frames indexed to the plant clock. The incident clip is continuous from 13:00:00 to 13:24:10. Vertical reference marks were surveyed before extraction. This report concerns vertical motion only.

D07.S02 Measured interval
Between 13:00:00 and 13:24:00, yoke downward displacement is 40 +/- 1 mm and carrier downward displacement is 0 +/- 1 mm. The defined seated start was visible at 13:00. Post/spreader contact remained visible during this interval. Displacements share the same reference frame and time window.

D07.S03 Release
At 13:24:03 the carrier starts downward travel into the pit. The keeper-to-yoke interface and lateral offset are occluded during the release. The clip cannot distinguish transient offset, rotation or local deformation as the keeper-bypass mechanism.

D07.S04 Coverage limits
No contact from an overhead crane or its load is visible within the fully covered carrier envelope from 13:00 to 13:24:03. Temporal and spatial resolution are sufficient to detect direct crane/load contact within that envelope during this interval. Coverage does not exclude an earlier disturbance or all conceivable contact outside that envelope. Measurement uncertainty is bounded as stated; it is not a confidence percentage.

D08.title: C17 boundary measurements - incident interval
D08.content:
D08.S01 Identity and time
Tags verified against C17/V17 in D02 and the WP-031 tag schedule. The records cover 13:00:00 to 13:24:00 on 14 October 2024, synchronized with CAM-3. They do not use the circuit nickname as identity.

D08.S02 Measured quantities
V17 CLOSED indication remains 1. The calibrated meter on the only C17-to-return route through V17 records 0.400 +/- 0.010 litres leaving the chamber. External loss is below 0.002 litres; the boundary inspection finds no alternate return route. Instrument checks passed before and after this interval.

D08.S03 Model limits
Use 100 cm2 effective area and 1:1 cylinder-to-yoke travel. Within this specified boundary, compression and temperature effects are negligible within the stated uncertainty. No independent block was present. Do not generalize these simplifications to an unspecified machine.

D08.S04 Interpretation boundary
The meter records chamber fluid leaving through the tagged route despite closed-position indication. It does not establish valve wear age, contamination, prior inspection decisions or why the carrier bypassed its keeper.

D09.title: V17 removed-valve examination and bench test
D09.content:
D09.S01 Custody
Valve tag V17 was photographed before removal after the event and retained in a sealed parts bag. No seat adjustment or cleaning preceded testing. Custody supports component identity, not a timestamp for every defect.

D09.S02 Test conditions and results
At the specified loaded-direction differential used for this fixture, the handle and limit switch indicated CLOSED. Reverse leakage measured 17 +/- 2 mL/min on three repeats. The external body did not leak. A later examination shows seat contamination; its arrival time is unknown.

D09.S03 Scope
This later test establishes bench behavior at examination and is compatible with the incident-route measurement. It alone does not establish the earlier leakage rate or prove when contamination developed. A successful later functional test would likewise not exclude every earlier intermittent condition.

D05.title: WP-031 - configuration and isolation execution record
D05.content:
D05.S01 Configuration entries
At 12:52 backup rolls were removed. At 12:57 the balance was raised. At 13:00 electrical isolation was recorded complete and the V17 handle was recorded CLOSED. These entries establish reported execution, not valve tightness.

D05.S02 Restraint observation
A configuration photograph taken at 13:00 and reviewed against the block locations shows no independent positive block under YK-3. The carrier is in contact with the mill post/spreader. The photo does not resolve keeper overlap.

D05.S03 Verification coverage
No loaded hold test, chamber-volume test or keeper-envelope check was recorded before work began. The absence of these entries does not prove deliberate noncompliance or explain the origin of any component defect.

D06A.title: Witness account W-A - pit-side observation
D06A.content:
D06A.S01 Vantage and timing
W-A observed from the pit-side access point between about 13:10 and 13:20. The carrier was visible against a fixed post mark. The yoke and cylinder were obscured.

D06A.S02 Account
The carrier looked stationary against the post mark while I watched. I could not see the yoke. I did not see the final release.

D06A.S03 Limits
This account cannot establish yoke position, hydraulic sealing or the exact time that carrier motion began. Approximate recollection is not a synchronized displacement measurement.

D06B.title: Witness account W-B - drive-side observation
D06B.content:
D06B.S01 Vantage and timing
W-B observed the yoke guide from the drive side near 13:20. The carrier/post contact and keeper were obscured.

D06B.S02 Account
The yoke was lower than its earlier chalk reference. I could not tell whether the carrier had moved with it. I heard the impact later.

D06B.S03 Limits
The observer cannot quantify displacement or identify the release path. A moving yoke and a stationary carrier are compatible observations of different objects.

D03A.title: R3 carrier and yoke - arrangement register
D03A.content:
D03A.S01 Document control
Status: superseded by revision C before 14 October 2024. Applicability: normal rolling arrangement, backup rolls installed, carrier seated and centered.

D03A.S02 Arrangement
This arrangement includes a backup-roll-associated stop. Centered keeper contact is shown; full offset travel is not qualified.

D03A.S03 Boundary
Do not infer that the backup-roll-associated stop remains present when backup rolls are removed. No maintenance-state travel envelope is specified.

D03C.title: R3 carrier and yoke - maintenance arrangement register
D03C.content:
D03C.S01 Document control
Status: current for the incident configuration. Equipment identifiers CB-3/YK-3. Backup rolls removed; carrier initially raised and seated on the yoke.

D03C.S02 Arrangement
The backup-roll-associated stop is absent in this configuration. No separate travel stop is fitted to prevent the raised carrier from reaching mill post/spreader interference. One keeper plate is fitted.

D03C.S03 Retention limits
The current record specifies 30 mm primary vertical seating engagement from the defined initial seat. Centered, seated keeper overlap is 8 mm. No approved off-center dynamic keeper-envelope calculation is contained in this revision.

D03C.S04 Interpretation
An intact installed keeper is not evidence that overlap is maintained at every lateral position. The absence of an envelope calculation describes a knowledge boundary; it does not itself cause physical motion.

D10.title: CB-3/YK-3 clearance and engagement review
D10.content:
D10.S01 Inputs
Use current revision C, a 30 mm initial primary seat, and the signed convention: positive means downward travel. Relative withdrawal equals yoke travel minus carrier travel. Bounded errors are combined by interval arithmetic, not by assuming independence.

D10.S02 Seated check
At the centered, seated post-event inspection position the keeper overlap is 8 +/- 1 mm. Under the rigid centered seated geometry, simple vertical passage over the yoke is not possible. This test does not reproduce the incident offset or rotation.

D10.S03 Open calculation
The incident lateral offset and release rotation are not measured. An approved off-center dynamic retention envelope is unavailable. Primary seating loss can be assessed from supplied vertical data; keeper bypass cannot be resolved from that calculation alone.

D10.S04 Required follow-up
Obtain a time-relevant lateral/rotation measurement or a validated retention-envelope analysis with an independently bounded incident offset. Repeating the centered seated measurement without new scope does not answer the dynamic question.

D14.title: Recovered assembly - condition inspection
D14.content:
D14.S01 Custody and examination
CB-3 and YK-3 were photographed after recovery. Keeper fasteners remain installed and the plate remains attached. The full plate and fasteners show no gross separation or fracture. This inspection does not establish dynamic overlap during release.

D14.S02 Condition
Witness marks are present on the carrier and mill post/spreader contact surfaces. The marks are consistent with contact but cannot alone date when contact began or establish the exact load carried.

D14.S03 Limits
No material record supports a fatigue-fracture explanation of a keeper bolt in this examination. Unmeasured deformation and the off-center release path remain separate questions.

D12.title: Investigation records desk - availability response
D12.content:
D12.S01 Available
Current maintenance arrangement C and superseded arrangement A are available. Requests for video, hydraulic measurements and bench records receive separate availability responses from the record custodian.

D12.S02 Unavailable
The incident keeper interface is not visible in another camera. No measured lateral offset at release or approved dynamic keeper-envelope analysis can be supplied from the retained records. No record establishes the contamination onset.

D12.S03 Reopening conditions
A newly validated envelope calculation plus a bounded incident offset could reopen the keeper branch. A traceable earlier contamination sample or dated inspection could reopen origin timing. This response establishes availability only; missing records are not physical causes.

D13.title: R3 corrective-action proposal register
D13.content:
D13.S01 Proposals
Propose a travel stop for the backup-roll-removed configuration; review keeper coverage through offset travel; evaluate a positive raised-yoke block; replace V17; review stored-energy controls.

D13.S02 Status
All entries are Identified. Effectiveness criteria have not been checked and implementation is not documented in this register.

D13.S03 Limit
A proposed modification is not evidence that the existing feature was absent, that its absence caused this event, or that the proposed design has been validated.

record.claim: D01 reports that the keeper plate was found bolted to the recovered assembly and that the beam and yoke were not reported fractured; these are initial observations, not a conclusion about the release mechanism.

D04 states that WP-031 for the raised balance assembly called for electrical supply isolation and hydraulic valve closure, and contained no instruction to install a positive yoke block or verify the off-center carrier retention envelope.

For R3 CB-3/YK-3 in the maintenance configuration, YK-3 follows C17 at a 1:1 vertical displacement ratio; with no independent mechanical block, loss of C17 support-chamber fluid can permit downward yoke travel under load, while V17 CLOSED/handle position or motor/pump isolation does not by itself prove seat sealing or mechanical restraint.

In the defined seated starting state, 30 mm of relative yoke-down withdrawal eliminates primary vertical seating, but keeper bypass additionally depends on lateral offset and dynamic path; mill post/spreader contact can temporarily hold the carrier while the yoke moves and is not a designed mechanical block.
At or before the 13:24 fall, C17 support-chamber fluid loss through V17 or another path caused or permitted yoke descent under load.
At the time of the fall, no effective positive yoke block or other independent mechanical restraint prevented yoke descent, or any restraint present was bypassed or ineffective.
At or before the fall, yoke downward travel exceeded carrier downward travel by at least 30 mm over the same interval, eliminating primary vertical seating engagement.

During the release, keeper engagement was bypassed or ineffective because lateral offset and the dynamic path allowed the carrier to separate despite the keeper plate later being found bolted to the recovered assembly.

A hydraulic/yoke-descent release path to the reported carrier fall would require the incident conditions of effective support loss/yoke descent, no effective independent restraint, sufficient relative withdrawal to lose primary seating, and keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path conditions allowing release; these conditions are not yet all supported.
A V17 CLOSED/handle-status indication by itself proves that the C17 support chamber was sealed against seat leakage or that trapped support fluid could not leave the chamber.
The keeper plate being found bolted to the recovered assembly by itself establishes that keeper bypass or release past the keeper could not have occurred during the incident.

Between 13:00:00 and 13:24:00 on 14 October 2024, from a visible defined seated start, YK-3/yoke moved downward 40 +/- 1 mm in the same reference frame while the carrier moved downward 0 +/- 1 mm; at 13:24:03 the carrier started downward travel into the pit.

From 13:00:00 to 13:24:00 on 14 October 2024, post/spreader contact remained visible while the yoke descended 40 +/- 1 mm and the carrier did not measurably descend; this supports a temporary interference/holding condition for the relative withdrawal but is not a designed mechanical block and does not establish keeper bypass.

Visible post/spreader contact is a candidate contributing condition to the measured relative yoke-down withdrawal because D02 states such contact can temporarily hold the carrier while the yoke moves downward and D07 shows the contact remained visible while the yoke descended and the carrier did not measurably descend; this does not by itself establish keeper bypass or the complete release path.
Direct overhead-crane or crane-load contact within D07's fully covered carrier envelope from 13:00:00 to 13:24:03 caused or triggered the carrier release.

After primary vertical seating was eliminated, a transient lateral offset of the carrier relative to the yoke/keeper allowed the carrier to clear or miss effective keeper engagement during the 13:24 release.

After primary vertical seating was eliminated, carrier rotation or tilt during release changed the keeper engagement path enough to permit separation despite the keeper plate later being found bolted.

Local elastic or plastic deformation of the carrier, yoke, keeper plate, bolts, or adjacent contact surfaces made keeper engagement ineffective during release without requiring a gross beam or yoke fracture.

The keeper was bolted but not in an effective retention geometry for the incident configuration because of orientation, installed position, bolt/slot condition, wear, or clearance relative to the off-center carrier path.

Any one or combination of transient lateral offset, carrier rotation/tilt, local deformation, or ineffective as-found keeper geometry could supply the unresolved keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path condition needed after primary seating loss; current evidence does not distinguish among them.

Given D02's 1:1 C17/YK-3 displacement ratio and 100 cm2 effective support area, D07's 40 +/- 1 mm YK-3 downward movement corresponds to approximately 0.39-0.41 L of C17 support-chamber volume decrease if the descent was C17 hydraulic movement.
During the raised parked interval before the fall, C17 support-chamber fluid escaped through V17 seat leakage despite any CLOSED handle/limit indication, permitting C17/YK-3 descent under load.

During the raised parked interval before the fall, C17 support-chamber fluid was lost externally from the support chamber or connected boundary at a quantity/rate sufficient to permit the measured C17/YK-3 descent.

During the raised parked interval before the fall, C17 support-chamber fluid left through an alternate chamber-to-return or hydraulic path other than V17 seat leakage, permitting C17/YK-3 descent under load.

Any one or combination of V17 seat leakage, external leakage, or an alternate chamber-to-return path could supply the unresolved C17 support-fluid-loss mechanism for the measured yoke descent if incident hydraulic records show sufficient pressure decay, flow, leakage, or volume balance; current evidence does not distinguish or confirm these paths.

The supported incident hydraulic path is C17 support-chamber fluid leaving through the V17 route despite CLOSED indication; this path supplies the measured volume needed for yoke descent, while sufficient external leakage and sufficient alternate return-path loss are refuted within D08's stated boundary and D09 remains only compatible later component evidence.

The hydraulic/yoke-descent path now has supported incident conditions for C17/V17 support-fluid loss, no effective independent positive restraint, and at least 30 mm relative yoke-down withdrawal eliminating primary seating; the complete causal path to the carrier fall remains candidate because keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path release is still unresolved.

During WP-031 execution before the fall, backup rolls were removed, the balance was raised, electrical isolation was recorded complete, V17 handle was recorded CLOSED, a 13:00 configuration photograph showed no independent positive block under YK-3, and no loaded hold test, chamber-volume test, or keeper-envelope check was recorded.

The photographed absence of an independent positive YK-3 block during WP-031 execution contributed to the available unrestrained yoke-descent condition because C17 support-fluid loss could move the yoke under load without a separate mechanical block; this does not establish the origin of the V17 leak or the keeper-release path.

WP-031 did not require installation or verification of an independent positive yoke block, and execution records show no such block present; this contributed to the unrestrained yoke-descent condition by not supplying a required mechanical-restraint control, without establishing deliberate noncompliance or the reason for the procedural omission.

For the incident maintenance configuration, revision C applies to CB-3/YK-3 with backup rolls removed; the backup-roll-associated stop is absent, no separate travel stop is fitted to prevent the raised carrier from reaching mill post/spreader interference, one keeper plate is fitted, primary vertical seating engagement is 30 mm, centered seated keeper overlap is 8 +/- 1 mm, and no approved off-center dynamic keeper-envelope calculation is available.

The maintenance configuration lacking the backup-roll-associated stop and lacking a separate travel stop contributed to the availability of mill post/spreader interference while the carrier was raised; D05/D07 show contact and D14 shows compatible contact marks, but this condition is not a designed mechanical block and does not by itself establish keeper bypass.

A later examination of removed V17 showed seat contamination, but the available evidence does not establish whether that contamination was present during the 13:00-13:24 incident interval, when it arrived, or what upstream maintenance/inspection condition caused it.

V17 seat contamination observed in later examination could have contributed to the supported V17 closed-route leakage if it was present during the incident, but current records do not date the contamination or establish its upstream origin.

D13 proposes a travel stop for the backup-roll-removed configuration, keeper coverage review through offset travel, evaluation of a positive raised-yoke block, V17 replacement, and stored-energy-control review; these entries are identified proposals only and are not evidence that the existing feature was absent, that its absence caused the event, or that a proposed design was implemented or validated.
Superseded arrangement revision A by itself establishes that the backup-roll-associated stop remained present and effective in the 14 October 2024 backup-roll-removed maintenance configuration.

Acquire WP-031 development, approval, stored-energy hazard review, and governing-control records to determine why positive yoke blocking, loaded hold or chamber-volume testing, and off-center keeper-envelope verification were not required for the raised CB-3/YK-3 backup-roll-removed task; an applicable documented design/procedure decision or standards gap would support an upstream procedural-control origin, a contrary applicable requirement or authorized deviation record would challenge the current omission-origin allocation, and unavailable records would leave the reason unresolved without changing the supported absence/omission finding.

Source basis: D07 reports a visible seated start, yoke down 40 +/- 1 mm, carrier down 0 +/- 1 mm, post/spreader contact visible, and carrier release at 13:24:03; D02 states >=30 mm relative withdrawal eliminates primary seating but keeper engagement additionally depends on lateral offset and dynamic path; D01’s bolted keeper/no reported fracture observations do not resolve engagement during release.

Disposition for targets N-MECH-YOKEDESC-001, N-MECH-HYD-001, and R-HYD-001: D07 supports the incident condition that YK-3 descended 40 +/- 1 mm while the carrier did not measurably descend before release. Under D02’s 1:1 C17/YK-3 behavior and 100 cm2 effective support area, that is hydraulically consistent with about 0.39–0.41 L of C17 support-chamber volume decrease if C17 movement supplied the descent: 100 cm2 x 3.9–4.1 cm = 390–410 cm3. This supports a necessary quantitative discriminator for hydraulic support loss, not occurrence of a hydraulic leak/flow path. N-MECH-HYD-001 should remain unresolved because no C17 pressure trend, V17 seat-leak/flow result, external-leak finding, alternate-return-path monitoring, pump/isolation implementation, or applicable post-event test sensitivity is supplied. Priority discriminators remain the existing R-HYD-001 fields, refined by D07’s measured interval and volume/rate implication. A pressure decay or measured chamber-to-return/external/alternate flow sufficient to account for roughly 0.4 L over the 13:00–13:24 interval would support hydraulic support loss; a preserved, sensitive, applicable negative test covering those paths and the incident boundary would challenge it; unavailable or insensitive results preserve the unresolved status. V17 CLOSED/handle indication alone remains inconclusive under D02 and refuted inference N-INF-HANDLE-001.

Admit both completed specialist submissions. They are not competing and are not an explanation-level merge: the retention-geometry proposal decomposes the still-unresolved keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path condition, while the hydraulic proposal decomposes the still-unresolved C17 fluid-loss origin and adds a quantitative discriminator from D07. D07 supports measured yoke descent and primary seating loss, but it expressly occludes the keeper interface and supplies no C17/V17 pressure, leakage, flow, or test evidence. Therefore N-MECH-KEEP-001 and N-MECH-HYD-001 remain unresolved; proposed subpaths are admitted only as candidates. Existing R-INSP-001 and R-HYD-001 are reused and refined; no duplicate acquisition is opened. No further specialist/assessor work is ready on the unchanged source set; the investigation waits for retained inspection, hydraulic, and execution/restraint records.

calls.decision: New evidence materially changes the hydraulic/support-loss and execution-restraint branches while leaving the keeper-release path unresolved. D08 supplies incident-time, synchronized C17/V17 boundary measurements: V17 indicated CLOSED but 0.400 +/- 0.010 L left the C17 chamber through the V17 route between 13:00 and 13:24, with external loss below 0.002 L and no alternate return route found. Using D02's 100 cm2 area and 1:1 C17/YK-3 relation, D07's 40 +/- 1 mm yoke descent implies about 0.39-0.41 L volume decrease, matching D08. This supports C17 fluid loss through the V17 closed route as the support-loss mechanism for yoke descent, while refuting sufficient external-loss or alternate-return-path routes within D08's stated boundary. D09 later bench testing is compatible with the V17 leakage route but does not by itself time the contamination or establish its upstream origin. D05 and D08 support that no independent positive yoke block was present; D05 also records electrical isolation and V17 handle CLOSED, which remain distinct from hydraulic sealing. D03C/D10/D14/D12 improve the configuration and inspection branch: current maintenance configuration had no backup-roll-associated stop or separate travel stop, one keeper, 30 mm primary seating, and 8 +/- 1 mm centered seated keeper overlap; centered seated geometry does not reproduce the incident offset/rotation, post-recovery inspection does not establish dynamic overlap, and no retained lateral-offset measurement or approved dynamic keeper-envelope analysis is available. Therefore the complete fall path remains candidate rather than fully supported because the keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path condition is still unresolved. D13 is only a corrective-action proposal register and is not treated as proof of occurrence, causation, validation, or implementation.

Admit the source-revision-16 assessor proposal with one semantic adjustment: the V17 contamination-timing record is entered as a supported evidence-boundary finding, not as proof that contamination caused the incident leak. D08/D09 answer R-HYD-001 and support C17 support-fluid loss through the V17 route despite CLOSED indication; D08 refutes sufficient external-loss and alternate-return routes within its stated boundary. D05/D08 answer R-EXEC-001 and support absence of an independent positive yoke block. D03C/D10/D12/D14 partially answer R-INSP-001 but preserve the unresolved keeper/lateral-offset/dynamic-path bridge. The complete hydraulic/yoke-descent fall path remains candidate because primary seating loss and hydraulic descent are supported but keeper release past the bolted keeper is not established. No duplicate requests are opened; no ready evidence or specialist job remains on the current record set. Reopening would require a newly validated dynamic retention-envelope analysis with bounded incident offset/rotation, or traceable dated contamination/origin evidence.

Upstream coverage review completed for the targeted supported premises. N-MECH-HYD-001 is explained at the immediate mechanism level by supported C17 fluid loss through the V17 route: D08 records 0.400 +/- 0.010 L leaving through V17 during 13:00-13:24, matching D07/D02's 0.39-0.41 L yoke-descent volume implication. N-MECH-HYD-V17LEAK-001 is therefore supported as an incident leakage route, but its component/upstream origin is not explained; N-HYD-CONTAM-001 is an evidence-boundary finding only because D09 later observed contamination but D09/D12 do not date it or identify its source. Do not repeat that unavailable timing route unless a traceable earlier sample or dated inspection is supplied. N-MECH-REST-001 is immediately explained by N-EXEC-001 and N-PROC-001: D05 shows no positive block/no hold or volume test recorded and D04 did not require a positive block or off-center keeper-envelope verification. The reason WP-031 lacked these controls is not explained and is immediately relevant, so a scoped upstream procedure-basis evidence request is opened. N-CONFIG-001 is supported by D03C/D10/D12 as the incident maintenance configuration, but the design/change-control origin of no travel stop and no approved dynamic retention envelope is not explained; a scoped design-basis evidence request is opened. N-MECH-POSTCONTACT-001 is operationally explained by the no-travel-stop maintenance configuration plus D05/D07 visible contact, but upstream origin follows the configuration design-basis branch. N-MECH-RELWD-001 is immediately explained by D07 yoke descent with carrier stationary, supported hydraulic descent, and visible post/spreader contact as a holding condition; no separate upstream branch is ready beyond the configuration/control requests. Keeper bypass remains unresolved and is not closed by this review.

calls.decision: R-PROC-UPSTREAM-001 is only partially answered. Search covered D01-D15 at collection revision 16. Fulfilled/usable coverage: D04.S01 shows WP-031 revision 3 covered the raised balance after backup-roll removal and called for electrical supply isolation plus hydraulic valve closure, with no instruction for positive yoke blocking or off-center carrier retention-envelope verification; D04.S02 ties the applicable tags to C17/V17; D04.S03 expressly says the package does not establish why the step was omitted. D05.S03 shows no loaded hold test, chamber-volume test, or keeper-envelope check was recorded before work began, but says that absence does not explain the origin. D13.S01-S03 shows only later identified proposals to review stored-energy controls/evaluate positive block/review keeper coverage, not prior approval basis or implementation. D02.S01 and D02.S06 are functional-description limits, not operating/isolation or governing-control instructions. Remaining/unanswered fields: WP-031 authoring and approval history; stored-energy or raised-load hazard assessment; governing standard/checklist for positive mechanical blocking; documented basis for relying on electrical isolation and V17 closure; documented basis for omitting loaded hold/chamber-volume testing; documented basis for omitting off-center keeper-envelope verification; deviation/waiver/MOC records; and prior similar task history/lessons learned. No contrary applicable requirement or authorized deviation record was found in the supplied hits. No source explicitly states these upstream procedure-control records are unavailable, so the route is not blocked; search miss alone is not treated as unavailability.

R-CONFIG-UPSTREAM-001 is partially answered. Search covered D01-D15 at collection revision 16. Fulfilled/usable coverage: D03C.S01 identifies revision C as current for the incident CB-3/YK-3 backup-roll-removed configuration; D03C.S02 states the backup-roll-associated stop is absent, no separate travel stop is fitted to prevent raised-carrier mill post/spreader interference, and one keeper plate is fitted; D03C.S03 states 30 mm primary seating, centered seated keeper overlap of 8 mm, and no approved off-center dynamic keeper-envelope calculation contained in revision C; D03C.S04 warns that an intact keeper does not prove overlap at every lateral position. D03A.S01-S03 show superseded revision A applied to normal rolling with backup rolls installed, included a backup-roll-associated stop, and warns not to infer that stop remains when backup rolls are removed; this gives limited change-history context but not a revision C approval/change-control basis. D10.S02-S04 confirm the centered seated 8 +/- 1 mm check does not reproduce incident offset/rotation and that an approved off-center dynamic retention envelope is unavailable. D12.S01-S02 explicitly says current arrangement C and superseded arrangement A are available, and that no measured lateral offset at release or approved dynamic keeper-envelope analysis can be supplied from retained records. D13.S01-S03 contains only later corrective-action proposals for a travel stop and keeper-coverage review and is not evidence of prior design basis, causation, implementation, or validation. Remaining/unanswered fields: revision C design-basis and approval package; documented change-control rationale from revision A to revision C; risk/hazard review for raised maintenance state with backup rolls removed; decision basis for no separate travel stop; decision basis for one keeper plate and centered overlap; documented reason why no approved off-center/dynamic retention-envelope analysis existed; interface review for mill post/spreader interference; and MOC/waiver/nonconformance records affecting travel stops or retention geometry. Explicitly unavailable from retained records: an approved off-center dynamic keeper-envelope analysis and measured incident lateral offset (D12.S02; D10.S03). No source in the hits supplies a contrary applicable superseding design or unauthorized-alteration record. No source explicitly states all upstream design-basis, risk-review, MOC/waiver, or change-control records are unavailable, so the whole request is not blocked; search miss alone is not treated as unavailability.

Assessment of R-PROC-UPSTREAM-001 and R-CONFIG-UPSTREAM-001: both remain only partially answered. The retrieved records support the immediate occurrence findings already in the ledger: WP-031 omitted positive yoke blocking/loaded hold or chamber-volume testing/off-center keeper-envelope verification, execution records show no positive block or such checks, and revision C had no backup-roll-associated stop, no separate travel stop, one keeper, 30 mm primary seating, centered keeper overlap only, and no approved off-center dynamic retention-envelope calculation. Those immediate omissions/configuration facts and their existing immediate contribution edges remain compatible. However, the new coverage does not establish the upstream origin of either branch. D04/D05/D13 do not supply WP-031 authoring/approval, hazard-review, governing-standard, waiver/deviation/MOC, reliance-basis, or lessons-learned records explaining the procedural omissions. D03C/D03A/D10/D12/D13 do not supply revision C design-basis, change-control rationale, risk-review, interface review, or MOC/waiver records explaining the absence of travel-stop/dynamic-envelope controls; D10/D12 explicitly leave the dynamic keeper-envelope and incident lateral-offset data unavailable from retained records. D13 remains only a later proposal register, not proof of prior design basis, occurrence, implementation, validation, or causation. Therefore no new supported upstream causal contribution should be added; upstream procedural-control and configuration/design-control origins should be recorded as unresolved, while preserving the supported immediate findings.

Admit the completed assessor proposal for R-PROC-UPSTREAM-001 and R-CONFIG-UPSTREAM-001. The proposal correctly separates supported immediate omissions/configuration conditions from unresolved upstream origins. The two branches share an evidence-boundary problem but are not semantically equivalent: WP-031 procedure-control basis and revision C configuration/design-control basis are distinct propositions with different records and causal targets. No new evidence request is opened, and no repeat search is scheduled on the same D01-D15/source-revision-16 collection.
